events.description:
21st Sunday after Pentecost; Sunday Worship with Holy Communion

College Chaplain Matthew Marohl will deliver the sermon; presided by Associate College Chaplain Sarah Semmler Smith ’04 and assisted by Jonathan Madden ’20, Interim Cantor to the Student Congregation. The Manitou Singers will be conducted by Therees Hibbard, Associate Professor of Practice and Robert Scholz Endowed Chair in Music. Comprised of alto and soprano voices from the first-year class, the Manitou Singers is one of the most popular music organizations on the St. Olaf College campus. With a repertoire that ranges from sacred to secular to popular ballads, the 100-voice choir sings at the opening worship service of the college as well as at various campus functions throughout the year. The Chapel Ringers handbell choir will be conducted by Jill Mahr, Adjunct Instructor in Music. 

Sunday Worship is a time of inspiration and worship for body, mind, and spirit; a meaningful beginning to a new week. All are welcome!

Click the web link below to access streamed and archived services.
events.title: Sunday Morning Worship: 21st Sunday after Pentecost

events.description:
This year marks a special milestone: the 50th anniversary of the Hong Kierkegaard Library. In 1976, Howard and Edna Hong donated their Kierkegaard collection to St. Olaf College, and that gift became the library and research center that has served scholars, students, and friends from around the world ever since.
This year’s Julia Watkin Lecture will be presented by William McDonald, an Australian philosopher and Kierkegaard scholar, who will speak on “Ethical-Religious Attention.” He will look at Kierkegaard’s critique of distraction alongside Buddhaghosa, Simone Weil, and Iris Murdoch. This lecture is open to the public.
events.title: 50th Anniversary of the Hong Kierkegaard Library Lecture

events.description: The Buntrock Institute for Freedom and Community invites the greater campus community to their Fall Speaker Series featuring Franita Tolson, Dean and Carl Mason Franklin Chair in Law, USC Gould School of Law, presenting In Congress We Trust? 250 Years of “We the Voters” in the American Democratic Experiment in Viking Theater on October 22 from 3:45-4:45 p.m. The lecture will focus on how Congress quietly shaped American elections across more than a century of constitutional development. In Congress We Trust? provides a new perspective on who truly governs our system of elections by showing that federal authority has been broad, lasting, and decisive.

events.description: History majors and students interested in pursuing a History major are welcome to attend the Career Fair with St. Olaf History Alumni, hosted by the St. Olaf History Department.  This event is an interactive career networking session featuring a diverse cohort of History alumni across various professional fields. The event will begin with brief introductions, where alumni will share overviews of their professional trajectories and industry insights. Following the introduction, the program will transition into an open networking session. Students are invited to circulate, speak one-on-one or in small groups with participating alumni, ask targeted career questions, and explore the versatile paths available to History graduates.  Pizza and soda will be provided.
events.title: Career Fair with St. Olaf History Alumni

events.description:
All are welcome to attend the Theater Department’s performances of Bakersfield Mist by Stephen Sachs, directed by Peter Hansen, and performed by St. Olaf students.

Maude, a fifty-something unemployed bartender, has bought a painting for a few bucks from the thrift store. Despite almost trashing it, she now thinks it’s a Jackson Pollock worth millions. But when world-class art expert, Lionel Percy, flies over from New York and arrives at her trailer park home in Bakersfield to authenticate the painting, he has no idea what he is about to discover. Inspired by true events, this sparkling and colorful new comedy-drama asks vital questions about what makes art and people truly authentic.
events.title: St. Olaf Theatre Department Presents — Bakersfield Mist
